title: Review: adversarial Opus 5.5 pass over the A5 integration PR
description:
READ-ONLY REVIEW. Do not edit, create, or delete any file; do not commit; do not push. Your only writes are bd notes on this bead and closing it.

SCOPE: the full diff of branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 against origin/main (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`) — one PR carrying eight beads: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (character suffocation recovery gate, migration 0032, set_suffocation, calc breath formulas), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (player-character death rules for encounter combatants, migration 0033), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.6 (adjust_hp knockOut), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3 (adjust_exhaustion, derived level-4 HP maximum, level-6 death), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4 (expend_ammunition / recover_ammunition, migration 0034), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3 (roll_retained_check / resolve_retained_check / end_retained_check, set_surprised derived from comparisons, migration 0035), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6 (hydra Multiple Heads curated mechanic, tracked head count, derived reaction allowance, migration 0036), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5 (action:use-an-object ordinaryInteractionRuleRef -> rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, importer). Run `bd show` on each bead and on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 for the specs and acceptance criteria.

AUTHORITY: AGENTS.md; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md (profile rules-clause-complete); ADR 0020 §§2-3 (dice, arithmetic, atomic state mutation, resource accounting, state integrity are deterministic; adjudicated outcomes still pass through those boundaries); docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendments A3-A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0015 (migration-first schema); docs/importer-fix-protocol.md for the importer parts; the committed SRD source text for every rule (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records use the `key` field).

METHOD (review the mechanism, not the narrative):
1. For each capability, print the governing SRD source text beside the implementation and check source fidelity of every engine rule (thresholds, tie semantics, rounding, ordering, what counts as damage/healing, lifecycle start/end).
2. Check every model-facing surface (tool descriptions, schemas, Hybrid Contract in protocol.ts, known-limit statements in ruleKnownLimits.ts, error/rejection messages) against the real code: truthful, no model-side arithmetic/comparison or model-held canonical state offered as a fallback, target domain correct (character vs combatant), no stale wording from the pre-capability disclosures.
3. State integrity: atomicity (single transaction), invariants across the full state space (alive/dying/stable/dead, monster vs player-character rules, recovery block, exhaustion levels, closed vs active combat instances, missing/malformed rows), concentration and attunement side effects, campaign-actor sync, provenance conventions, deterministic ids/replay, write paths that bypass established helpers (mutateState, claimItem, removeItem), migration correctness (constraints, indexes, data preservation, contiguity, schema snapshot).
4. Write paths that let a model persist an unsupported/derived value (the A5 forbidden-substitution class), and any place a refusal could be bypassed through another tool (e.g. add_condition, update_combatant status, rest, level-up).
5. Test evidence: does each acceptance criterion have a test that distinguishes the bad state from the good state? Name missing evidence only where a real requirement is unprotected.
6. Sibling search: for each defect, look for the same class elsewhere in the diff.

REPORT with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this bead>`. One entry per finding: ID (S1, S2, ...), severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), file:line, the violated requirement and its authority, a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> wrong state), and the minimal fix. Then a short list of what you checked and found correct. Apply the review policy's "From observation to finding" test: an observation without an operative requirement is "no requirement" in one line, not a finding. Do not stop at the first defect; batch everything you can find.

SIXTH PASS (adversarial Opus 5.5 reviewer; Sol is unavailable). Prior Sol reviews: eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1, .8.4, .8.6, .8.8, .8.11 (read all; the latest, .8.11, lists S24, S25, S27-S34 as open). Since .8.11: Sonnet repair batches F1 (.8.12, combatant side) and F2 (.8.13, character side), and a supervisor commit making updateCombatant resolve the creature record only for HP changes and threading the resolver through begin_turn/close_combat_instance effect settlement. (1) State CLOSED/OPEN for S24, S25, S27, S28, S29, S30, S31, S32, S33, S34 with fresh adversarial evidence. (2) Be adversarial: actively try to break the lifecycle transition function (state/combatantLifecycle.ts), the character HP lifecycle (state/hpLifecycle.ts), actor persistence/projection, ammunition accounting, retained checks/surprise, and exhaustion — construct sequences through the real tool registry, not only unit calls. (3) Fresh full review of the rest of the PR (IDs from S35). Apply "From observation to finding" strictly: no speculative robustness findings. Close with APPROVE-READY or CHANGES REQUESTED.
acceptance_criteria: Closure states plus any new findings recorded in bd notes with an overall disposition; no file changes; bead closed by the reviewer.
notes:
SIXTH PASS (adversarial Opus 5.5), bound to HEAD 538d8625, origin/main ae840498; rules-clause-complete. Probes are throwaway /tmp/rv14 scripts driving createDefaultToolRegistry().invoke; one parity probe imports the parent checkout (origin/main) read-only.

S35 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/combatantLifecycle.ts:274 (damage branch, monster rules: dead only when oldHp>0); locked in by packages/core/test/combatantLifecycle.test.ts:700 ('monster knocked out: further damage stays unconscious')
Requirement/authority: .19.5.7.5 acceptance 'default behavior unchanged ... default dead-at-0 preserved'; batch-E D2 names pre-PR behaviour as the monster-rules reference; SRD rule:monsters-and-death (monsters die at 0 rather than following PC rules) + rule:knocking-a-creature-out ('falls unconscious and is stable'; a stable creature taking damage at 0 HP re-enters the death-save track, which monster rules replace with death). update_combatant description still promises 'an hpDelta that brings the combatant to 0 hit points sets it dead unless status is also passed'. ADR 0020 §3 lifecycle is deterministic.
Failure through registry (S29 repair restored the knockout, but its follow-on state is new): goblin 7/7 -> update_combatant(hpDelta:-10,status:unconscious) -> 0/unconscious (correct). Then update_combatant(hpDelta:-5) and (hpDelta:-5,critical:true) both succeed and leave 0 HP/unconscious/monster forever. Same sequence on origin/main (parent checkout): the follow-up hit commits dead. Silent outcome change; the model receives ok and no signal. Sibling (same branch, same root cause): healing that knocked-out monster (hpDelta:+3) leaves status unconscious at 3 HP although SRD rule:falling-unconscious says 'This unconsciousness ends if you regain any hit points' — main also kept 'unconscious' here, so the heal half is pre-existing and is noted only as the fix's adjacent edge, not separately required.
Minimal fix: in the monster-rules damage branch, treat positive damage to a creature already at 0 HP whose status is unconscious (the knockout result) as death (no death saves under monster rules), preserving the terminal-cause and head paths; correct the matrix row at test:700. Optionally (same transition) let positive actual regain from 0 HP clear knockout unconsciousness.
Permanent evidence: generalized — amend the existing ordinary-state matrix row(s) for monster unconscious@0 x {damage, critical damage} -> dead, and keep the S29 knockout row; no new reproducer file. Proportionate: one row-class of the D9 matrix that currently asserts the wrong outcome.
Owner: combatant lifecycle (F1 area). Material behaviour repair; required next state: fix before approval.
S36 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:587-588 (dying/stable combatant => unavailableReason, turn completed and end-of-turn settled inside the same begin_turn, :956-987); packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolBeginTurn.ts:21 (description lists only dead/escaped/inactive as turnAvailable:false)
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:death-saving-throws ('Whenever you start your turn with 0 hit points, you must make a special saving throw'); creature:hydra Multiple Heads regrows/heals 'At the end of its turn'; .19.5.7.5 requires the combatant dying lifecycle to MIRROR the character death rules (a dying character's turn stays available: actionEconomy.ts:609-614 marks only dead characters unavailable); .19.3.4.6 full head lifecycle; ADR 0020 §3 owns lifecycle ordering. Protocol tells the model to 'roll a d20 each of their turns and record it with record_death_save'.
Failure through registry: hydra opted into PC rules -> update_combatant(hpDelta:-172) => dying 0 HP, 4 heads, 1 head owed; record_death_save(5) => F1. Next round begin_turn(hydra, round:2): the dying participant is 'unavailable', so the same call completes its turn and runs end-of-turn regrowth => alive 20 HP, 6 heads, counters reset, turnAvailable:false. The start-of-turn death save the protocol requires is then refused ('only a dying player-character combatant may make death saves'). With F2 instead of F1, SRD order (start-of-turn save first, regrowth at turn end) kills the hydra on a 1-9; the engine deterministically revives it. Characters and combatants also diverge (dying character turn available, dying combatant not). The begin_turn description does not disclose dying/stable as unavailable nor any 'record the death save first' ordering, so the model cannot avoid this from the contract.
Minimal fix: give a dying PC-rules combatant an available turn (its start-of-turn death save is recorded inside its turn; end-of-turn settlement — head regrowth, turn-end effects — runs at the next begin_turn as for any available participant), keeping stable/dead/escaped/inactive skip semantics; or, if the skip is retained by explicit decision, run end-of-turn settlement only after the turn's death save has been recorded and state that ordering in begin_turn/record_death_save. Update the begin_turn description to match whichever is accepted.
Permanent evidence: generalized — extend the existing own-turn settlement/S27 actionEconomy coverage with a dying PC-rules hydra carrying 2 failures and an owed head: start-of-turn failing save => dead with no regrowth; passing save => regrowth at turn end. Proportionate to an ordering defect that flips survival.
Owner: .19.5.7.5/.19.3.4.6 integration (turn boundary). Material behaviour repair; required next state: fix (or explicit supervisor decision recorded in a bead) before approval.
S34 | OPEN (character half CLOSED; combatant half repaired only in the pure transition, not in its persistence adapter) | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:2098-2104 (resolveCombatantDeathSave needsSchedule = roll !== 20 && roll >= 10 && successes >= 2 && unblocked), :2114-2119 (outcome label)
Requirement/authority: unchanged from .8.11 S34 (rule:death-saving-throws third success => stable, counters reset; F1 supervisor decision: zero-regain natural 20 counts through the SAME capped-success path so a third success stabilizes with an armed schedule; character/combatant parity).
Fresh registered evidence: PC-rules goblin 1/1 -> adjust_exhaustion(delta:4, combatantId) => dying 0/eff 0 -> record_death_save 12, 12, 20: the third call is REFUSED 'stabilizing requires a seeded recovery schedule' and rolls back (dying, successes 2). The pure transition (combatantLifecycle.ts:331-345) now takes the success path but the adapter never seeds a schedule for roll 20, so the transition refuses. Further consequence: the creature can never stabilize on that roll and a later failure can kill it. Siblings: 12,12,12 at eff 0 stabilizes, settles at 241 min, re-arms on adjust_exhaustion(-1) and recovers 1 HP (correct); the character domain with 12,12,20 stabilizes (dl 180), settles, re-arms and recovers (correct, CLOSED). Also the returned outcome for that nat-20 would read 'success' even when it stabilizes (label branch at :2114 ignores lifecycle.status).
Evidence gap that let it through: combatantLifecycle.test.ts:1068 calls nextCombatantLifecycle with a schedule always supplied, so it cannot observe the adapter's gate; no registry/adapter test covers zero-max nat 20 for combatants.
Minimal fix: seed the schedule whenever the transition may stabilize (roll >= 10 incl. 20 when it cannot regain HP — or simply whenever roll >= 10 && successes >= 2 && unblocked), and derive outcome from lifecycle.status ('stabilized' when stable).
Permanent evidence: generalized — run the existing S34 last-roll x max x block table through resolveCombatantDeathSave (or record_death_save) rather than only the pure function, asserting status/counters/schedule. Owner: F1 combatant death-save adapter. Required next state: repair before approval.
S38 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1856-1862 (start_encounter projection status: hpCurrent === 0 under monster rules => 'dead'), then syncCombatantActor at :1934 writes the death back to the canonical actor
Requirement/authority: .19.5.7.5 'default behavior unchanged'; F1 supervisor decision for S29 (monster knockout = HP 0, status unconscious, NO death); SRD rule:knocking-a-creature-out ('falls unconscious and is stable'); batch-E D1/D4 (projection/admission is a lifecycle event that must not invent a death) and D9 actor/projection parity; ADR 0020 state integrity.
Failure through registry (fresh, both branches compared): goblin actor 7/7 -> update_combatant(hpDelta:-10,status:unconscious) => 0/unconscious (correct, actor synced 0/unconscious) -> close_combat_instance(completed) -> start_encounter(c2, actors:[{actorId:'gob'}]). Branch: new projection c2-gob is 0 HP/dead AND the campaign actor is rewritten to dead. origin/main (parent checkout): projection and actor stay 0/unconscious. The classic 'knock the bandit out, question him later' flow silently kills a persistent NPC on his next projection; nothing in the result signals a death.
Minimal fix: in the projection status derivation, keep an existing monster-rules actor whose status is 'unconscious' at 0 HP as unconscious (only an actor with no non-lethal 0-HP status — e.g. alive/unknown at 0 — derives dead), keeping terminal causes (exhaustion 6, zero heads) => dead and the PC-rules branch unchanged.
Permanent evidence: generalized — extend the existing projection/admission coverage (encounterCombatants or exhaustion actor-parity tests) with an actor status x profile table at 0 HP {unconscious-monster, dying/stable-PC, dead} asserting projection status AND actor status are preserved across close/reopen. Proportionate: canonical persistent-actor state.
Owner: combatant lifecycle / actor projection (F1 area). Required next state: repair before approval.

S37 | nit | packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolSetSurprised.ts:14 (description) vs :159-169 (mismatched_observer_sets)
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:surprise compares the Stealth of 'anyone hiding' with the passive Perception of 'each creature on the opposing side' — both sides may hide; .19.5.10.3 acceptance requires the set_surprised description to give a deterministic surprise path; review policy: model-facing contracts must be truthful.
Failure through registry: PC hides (retained check A compared with goblins g1,g2) and goblin g1 hides (retained check B compared with the PC). Following the description ('pass all resulting comparison ids here') => refused mismatched_observer_sets. Calling set_surprised once per side succeeds (A => g1,g2 surprised; B => pc surprised), but nothing tells the model to split. No state corruption; refusal only.
Minimal fix: one sentence in the description (call once per hiding side, passing that side's comparisons), or group the observer-set check by side. Permanent evidence: a tools.test description assertion is sufficient if the contract sentence is chosen; no new state test needed. Owner: .19.5.10.3.
S39 | nit | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts requireActiveCombatant (resolveCombatantDeathSave/stabilizeCombatant/setCombatantSuffocation) + packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolCloseCombatInstance.ts:18 (description)
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:stabilizing-a-creature (first aid on an unconscious creature, not limited to combat); .19.5.7.5 makes the combatant dying lifecycle engine-owned; A5 forbids model-held canonical state as a fallback; review policy: truthful model-facing contracts.
Observation through registry: PC-rules bandit captain actor dropped to 0 => dying; close_combat_instance(completed) leaves projection+actor dying. Afterwards record_death_save/stabilize_character(combatantId) refuse 'belongs to inactive combat instance' and advance_time(600) leaves it dying indefinitely. The only engine path is to start_encounter again with that actor (projects dying) and stabilize there — which works (stable, deadline armed) but is disclosed nowhere; start_encounter's own refusal text says 'use the lifecycle tools'. No corruption; a refusal plus an undocumented recovery path, so nit.
Minimal fix: disclose in close_combat_instance (or stabilize_character/record_death_save) that a dying PC-rules combatant should be resolved before closing, or that it is resolved by projecting the actor into a new encounter. Permanent evidence: none beyond a description assertion if the sentence is added. Owner: .19.5.7.5.
S40 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/combatantLifecycle.ts:497-499 (monster suffocationDrop => dead with recoveryBlock null) + :153-165 (D2 ordinaryMonsterHealing exception has no suffocation cause); packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolSetSuffocation.ts:20 (description)
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:suffocating ('it can't regain hit points or be stabilized until it can breathe again'); .19.5.7.5/.19.5.7.4 combatant suffocation gate (set_suffocation is the engine-owned gate, and its description promises the drop 'blocks healing and stabilization until event breathe'); batch-E D2 limits the dead-monster healing exception to ORDINARY death; method item 4 (refusal bypass through another tool); ADR 0020 state integrity.
Failure through registry: monster-rules goblin 7/7 -> set_suffocation(drop, combatantId) => 0 HP/dead, recovery_block NULL. update_combatant(hpDelta:+5) => alive 5/7 while the creature still cannot breathe; set_suffocation(breathe) then refuses 'no recovery block to clear'. The PC-rules sibling correctly refuses healing while suffocating. So the gate the tool description advertises is bypassed by ordinary healing for every monster-rules combatant, through the D2 revival path that was scoped to ordinary death.
Minimal fix: make a monster-rules suffocation death not eligible for the D2 healing exception while the creature cannot breathe (e.g. treat it as a terminal cause like exhaustion 6/zero heads, or retain a dead-state suffocation marker that refuses positive regain until breathe), and make the set_suffocation description state the monster outcome exactly.
Permanent evidence: generalized — one more terminal/gated cause row in the existing D2/terminal-priority matrix (monster suffocation death x heal => refusal) plus the registered drop->heal refusal; proportionate to a recovery-gate bypass.
Owner: combatant suffocation/D2 (F1 area). Required next state: repair (or explicit recorded supervisor decision that monster suffocation death is ordinary revivable death, with the description corrected) before approval.

NO REQUIREMENT (one line each): retained_check/comparison ids are random UUIDs — no authority requires deterministic ids for these rows and turn replay is snapshot-hash based; heal of a knocked-out monster leaving 'unconscious' is pre-existing main behaviour (noted inside S35); adjust_exhaustion's character result omits concentrationBroken although the break happens — no contract requires reporting it; D2 dead-monster revival by healing contradicts SRD rule:healing but is an explicit accepted supervisor decision preserving main behaviour (flagged for awareness, not a finding; S40 covers its suffocation bypass only).

CHECKED AND FOUND CORRECT (subject to the entries above): nextCombatantLifecycle damage/overflow/at-zero failures/critical, heal reset, deathSave capped-success/nat20/nat1, stabilize, PC knockout schedule, suffocation drop/breathe incl. counter preservation, exhaustionChanged clamp/level-6/re-arm, head death once per turn and zero-head death, regrowth count x 10 HP with fire suppression and dead exclusion, recoveryDue settle/recover, invariant tail; character hpLifecycle damage (temp HP first, overflow vs effective max, damage-at-0 instant death vs effective max), knockOut gates, healing gate while suffocating, death-save transition parity, level-up effective-max clamp; ammunition per-expenditure rows, floor-half per identity, custody via claimItem/destroyInventoryItem, once-only settlement, location guard; retained checks strict-greater notice, passive score via calc, surprise any-noticed => not surprised, per-observer completeness, combat-instance staleness; calc breath_hold_duration/suffocation_survival_rounds vs rule:suffocating; known-limit/protocol rewrites; migrations 0032-0038 (no FK references into rebuilt tables, data copied, constraints).
